p.src: They all said, “Our meeting today can hardly be chance. Brother Headman must take the seat of honor.” Chao Gai said, “I am merely your impoverished host. How could I dare take the highest place?” Wu Yong said, “Brother Headman is the eldest. If you will heed my humble opinion, please take your seat.” Chao Gai had no choice but to take the first seat. Wu Yong sat second, Gongsun Sheng third, Liu Tang fourth, Ruan Xiaoer fifth, Ruan Xiaowu sixth, and Ruan Xiaoqi seventh. They had only just assembled in fellowship and begun drinking, but now the cups and dishes were laid afresh, more wine and food were prepared, and all drank together. Wu Yong said, “The headman dreamed that the seven stars of the Northern Dipper fell upon his roof ridge, and today the seven of us have assembled in righteousness to undertake this deed. Is this not an omen sent down by Heaven? This fortune lies within easy reach. The other day we spoke of asking Brother Liu to scout the route by which they will come. It is late today, so please set out early tomorrow morning.” Gongsun Sheng said, “There is no need to go on that errand. I have already made inquiries and learned their route. They will come by the main road over Yellow Mud Ridge.” Chao Gai said, “Ten li east of Yellow Mud Ridge is a place called Anle Village. An idler named Bai Sheng, known as the ‘Daylight Rat,’ lives there. He once came to seek my protection, and I gave him money for his expenses.” Wu Yong said, “Could the white light upon the Northern Dipper have pointed to this very man? We shall indeed have use for him.” Liu Tang said, “Yellow Mud Ridge is some distance from here. Where can we find shelter?” Wu Yong said, “Bai Sheng’s house will serve as our lodging, and we shall need Bai Sheng himself as well.” Chao Gai said, “Master Wu, are we to take the treasure by guile or by force?” Wu Yong laughed and said, “I have already laid the trap. We shall judge the circumstances when they arrive: if force is called for, we shall take it by force; if wit is called for, we shall take it by wit. I have a plan, though I do not know whether it will meet with your approval. It goes like this...” When Chao Gai heard it, he was overjoyed. Stamping his foot, he cried, “What a marvelous plan! You truly deserve to be called the ‘Resourceful Star’! You surpass Zhuge Liang himself! An excellent plan!” Wu Yong said, “Say no more of it. As the proverb goes, ‘Walls are sure to have ears; how could there be no one beyond the window?’ This must remain known only to you and me.” Chao Gai then said, “You three Ruan brothers should return home for now and come to my humble manor on the appointed day. Master Wu may return to his teaching as usual. Master Gongsun and Liu Tang may stay here at my manor for the time being.” They drank until evening that day, then each retired to a guest room to rest.

p.src: The next day they rose at the fifth watch and ate the breakfast that had been prepared. Chao Gai brought out thirty taels of fine silver and presented it to the three Ruan brothers, saying, “This is but a small token of my regard. Please do not refuse it.” But the three Ruans would not accept it. Wu Yong said, “You must not turn aside a friend’s goodwill.” Only then did the three Ruans accept the silver. They all escorted them beyond the manor, where Wu Yong whispered in their ears, “Do thus and thus, and be sure there is no mistake when the appointed time comes.” The three Ruans took their leave and returned to Shijie Village. Chao Gai kept Gongsun Sheng and Liu Tang at his manor. Wu the Scholar came often to discuss their plans. Indeed:

p.src: Let us leave these details and speak instead of the Eastern Capital’s Daming Prefecture. Grand Secretary Liang had finished purchasing birthday gifts worth one hundred thousand strings of cash and chose a day to send his men on their journey. One day, while he was seated in the rear hall, Lady Cai asked him, “My lord, when will the birthday convoy set out?” Grand Secretary Liang replied, “The gifts are all ready. They are to set out tomorrow or the day after. There is only one matter over which I remain hesitant and undecided.” Lady Cai asked, “What matter has left you hesitant and undecided?” Grand Secretary Liang said, “Last year I spent one hundred thousand strings of cash purchasing gold, pearls, and precious objects to send to the Eastern Capital. But because I entrusted them to the wrong men, bandits seized them along the road, and to this day neither the goods nor the culprits have been recovered. This year, among all the men before me, I again see no capable person who can see the convoy safely through. That is why I remain undecided.” Pointing to a man below the steps, Lady Cai said, “You are always saying that this man is exceptionally capable. Why not appoint him, issue him written orders and a warrant of responsibility, and have him make the journey? Then nothing should go amiss.”

p.src: When Secretary Liang looked at the man below the steps, he saw that it was Yang Zhi, the Blue-Faced Beast. Secretary Liang was delighted. He immediately summoned Yang Zhi into the hall and said, “I had quite forgotten about you. If you can deliver the Birthday Gifts for me, I shall see that you are well advanced.” Yang Zhi stepped forward with clasped hands and replied, “I dare not disobey Your Excellency’s command! I merely do not know what preparations are to be made, or when we are to depart.” Secretary Liang said, “Have Daming Prefecture provide ten covered carts, and assign ten garrison soldiers from my command to escort them. Plant a yellow flag on each cart bearing the words ‘Birthday Gifts Presented in Congratulation to the Grand Preceptor.’ Assign another stout soldier to accompany each cart, and you must set out within three days.” Yang Zhi said, “It is not that I wish to shirk the duty, but the journey truly cannot be made that way. I beg Your Excellency to send another capable and circumspect man.” Secretary Liang said, “I intend to advance you. Among the official papers accompanying the Birthday Gifts, I shall place a separate letter strongly recommending you to the Grand Preceptor, so that you may return with an imperial appointment. Why do you raise objections and refuse to go?” Yang Zhi said, “Your Excellency, I have heard that last year’s gifts were seized by bandits, who remain uncaptured to this day. There are even more brigands on the roads this year. The route to the Eastern Capital has no waterways and lies entirely overland. It passes Zijin Mountain, Twin Dragon Mountain, Peach Blossom Mountain, Canopy Mountain, Yellow Mud Ridge, White Sand Hollow, Wild Cloud Ferry, and Red Pine Forest—all places frequented by outlaws. Even solitary travelers dare not pass those places alone. Once the outlaws learn that we carry gold, silver, and treasure, how could they fail to attack us? We would merely throw away our lives. That is why I cannot go.” Secretary Liang said, “In that case, simply send more officers and soldiers to guard the convoy.” Yang Zhi said, “Even if Your Excellency sent five hundred men, it would be no use. The moment those fellows hear that outlaws are coming, they will all be the first to flee.” Secretary Liang said, “If what you say is true, are the Birthday Gifts not to be sent at all?” Yang Zhi replied, “If Your Excellency will grant me one condition, I shall dare undertake the delivery.” Secretary Liang said, “Since I have entrusted the matter to you, of course I shall heed what you say.” Yang Zhi said, “If you follow my plan, we shall use no carts at all. We shall pack the gifts into a dozen or so carrying loads, dress as merchants, and pretend to be transporting ordinary wares. Choose ten sturdy garrison soldiers and disguise them as porters to carry the loads. Only one other man need accompany me, likewise disguised as a merchant. We shall travel quietly, even through the night, and deliver everything in the Eastern Capital. Only then will the plan be sound.” Secretary Liang said, “What you say is entirely right. I shall write a letter strongly recommending you, so that you may return with an imperial appointment.” Yang Zhi said, “I am deeply grateful for Your Excellency’s patronage.” That very day, Yang Zhi was ordered to prepare the loads and porters while selecting the soldiers.

p.src: The next day, Yang Zhi was summoned to wait before the hall. Secretary Liang came out and asked, “Yang Zhi, when will you depart?” Yang Zhi replied, “With Your Excellency’s permission, I shall leave tomorrow morning, as soon as I receive the warrant accepting custody.” Secretary Liang said, “My wife also has a load of gifts to be sent separately to her honored kin in the household, and you must take charge of it. For fear that you may not know the route, I have specially ordered Steward Xie, the Grand Preceptor’s former wet nurse’s husband, and two attendants to accompany you.” Yang Zhi said, “Your Excellency, then I cannot go.” Secretary Liang said, “All the gifts have already been securely packed. Why can you no longer go?” Yang Zhi replied, “The ten loads of gifts are entrusted entirely to me, and all the men are to obey me: if I order an early start, they start early; if I order a late start, they start late; if I tell them to halt or rest, they halt or rest. Everything must be under my direction. But now you are sending the old steward and the attendants with me. They belong to my lady’s household, and the steward is the husband of the Grand Preceptor’s former wet nurse. If they oppose me on the road, how could I dare contend with them? If the great affair should thereby miscarry, how could Yang Zhi explain himself then?” Secretary Liang said, “That is easily settled. I shall order all three of them to obey your direction.” Yang Zhi answered, “If that is formally declared, I am willing to accept the warrant at once. Should any mishap occur, I shall willingly bear the severest punishment.” Secretary Liang was overjoyed and said, “My efforts to advance you have not been wasted. You truly are a man of discernment!” He immediately summoned old Steward Xie and the two attendants and instructed them in the hall: “Commandant Yang Zhi has willingly signed a warrant accepting custody of the Birthday Gifts. He will escort eleven loads of gold, pearls, and treasure to the Grand Preceptor’s residence in the capital and deliver them there. The entire responsibility rests upon him. You three will accompany him. Throughout the journey—whether rising early, traveling late, halting, or resting—you must obey his words and must not oppose him. You three know how to handle the commission given by my wife. Be vigilant and careful, go swiftly and return swiftly, and allow nothing to go amiss.” The old steward agreed to every instruction.

p.src: Yang Zhi accepted the charge that day. At the fifth watch early the next morning, he arranged all the loads and carrying poles before the hall in the residence. The old steward and the two attendants brought another small load of valuables, making eleven loads in all. Eleven sturdy garrison soldiers were selected and dressed as porters. Yang Zhi put on a coolie hat and a blue gauze shirt, bound his leggings, and wore hempen traveling sandals. He girded a saber at his waist and carried a long-handled blade. The old steward likewise disguised himself as a merchant; the two attendants pretended to be merchant’s servants. Each man took a long-handled blade, and they also carried several rattan canes. Secretary Liang handed over the official papers and letters. After everyone had eaten his fill, they bade farewell to Secretary Liang in the hall. The soldiers shouldered the loads and set out. Escorted by Yang Zhi, Steward Xie, and the two attendants, the party of fifteen left the Liang residence, passed through the gates of Beijing, and took the main road toward the Eastern Capital. It was now the middle of the fifth month. Though the sky was beautifully clear, the fierce heat made travel difficult. In former times Prince Wu of the Seventh Commandery composed eight lines of verse: A jade screen is ringed on every side with vermilion rails; schools of darting fish play among the duckweed. An eight-foot mat of white shrimp-whisker bamboo is spread, and beneath the head lies a pillow of red agate. The six dragons fear the heat and dare not move; the sea boils around the isle of Penglai. Yet still the young lord finds his fan too weak, while travelers toil upon the red-dust road.

p.src: These eight lines speak solely of the scorching summer months. Princes and noble youths recline in cool pavilions and waterside chambers, chilling melons and plums in water and preparing ice and snowy lotus root to escape the heat, yet still complain of being hot. How could they know that travelers, pursuing some trifling fame and meager profit, though neither cangue nor fetters bind them, must journey along the roads even in the hottest days of summer? Yang Zhi and his party had to arrive in time for the birthday on the fifteenth day of the sixth month, and so they had no choice but to press onward. For five or seven days after leaving Beijing, they invariably rose at the fifth watch and traveled in the cool of early morning, resting when the midday heat arrived.

p.src: After five or seven days, dwellings gradually grew fewer, travelers became scarce, and each stage of the journey led along mountain roads. Yang Zhi, however, insisted on setting out at the Hour of the Dragon and stopping by the Hour of the Monkey. The eleven guardsmen had loads that were all equally heavy. In the heat they could go no farther, and whenever they saw a grove, they wanted to rest there. But Yang Zhi drove them on, continually urging them forward. If they stopped, he would curse them fiercely for a minor offense, and for a serious one beat them with his rattan switch, forcing them onward. Though the two attendants carried only a few bundles of luggage on their backs, they too were panting and unable to keep up. Yang Zhi rebuked them as well: “You two have no sense at all! The responsibility for this rests on me. Instead of helping me drive these porters along, you dawdle behind them yourselves. This road is no place for fooling around!” One attendant replied, “It is not that we two wish to walk slowly. The truth is that the heat makes it impossible to move, so we have fallen behind. Before, we always traveled in the cool of the early morning. Why must we now march in the fiercest heat? Your treatment is altogether uneven.” Yang Zhi said, “That talk of yours is nothing but wind! The roads we traveled before were safe country. Now we are in dangerous terrain. If we do not hurry through it by daylight, who would dare travel here in the dead of night?” The two attendants said nothing aloud, but thought to themselves, “That fellow has no cause to insult people so freely.”

Though the two attendants carried only a few bundles of luggage on their backs, they too were panting and unable to keep up.
Yang Zhi rebuked them as well: “You two have no sense at all!
The responsibility for this rests on me. Instead of helping me drive these porters along, you dawdle behind them yourselves.
This road is no place for fooling around!”
One attendant replied, “It is not that we two wish to walk slowly. The truth is that the heat makes it impossible to move, so we have fallen behind.
Before, we always traveled in the cool of the early morning. Why must we now march in the fiercest heat? Your treatment is altogether uneven.”
Yang Zhi said, “That talk of yours is nothing but wind!
The roads we traveled before were safe country. Now we are in dangerous terrain. If we do not hurry through it by daylight, who would dare travel here in the dead of night?”
The two attendants said nothing aloud, but thought to themselves, “That fellow has no cause to insult people so freely.”

p.src: Yang Zhi raised his long-handled sword, took up his rattan switch, and went off himself to drive the burden-bearers onward. The two attendants sat beneath the shade of a willow. When the old steward caught up, they complained to him: “That Yang fellow is, at most, merely an escort officer in our lord’s service, yet he puts on such airs of authority!” The steward said, “Our lord instructed me to my face not to quarrel with him, so I have kept silent. These past two days I too have found him intolerable, but let us endure him for now. The two attendants said, “Our lord spoke merely out of courtesy. You need only take matters into your own hands.” The old steward said again, “Let us bear with him a little longer.”

p.src: That day, at about the Hour of the Monkey, they found an inn and stopped for the night. The ten guardsmen were drenched in streaming sweat. Sighing and panting, they said to the old steward, “It was our misfortune to become soldiers, knowing full well that we would be sent out on assignments. But in weather hot as fire, carrying such heavy loads, we have not even been allowed to travel in the cool morning these past two days; and at the slightest thing that great rattan switch comes beating down upon us. We are all flesh born of parents—why must we suffer so cruelly?” The old steward said, “Do not harbor resentment. Once we reach the Eastern Capital, I shall reward you myself.” The soldiers said, “If we were treated as you treat us, Steward, we would not dare bear any resentment.” Another night passed.

p.src: Before dawn the next day, everyone rose, intending to set out while it was still cool. Yang Zhi sprang up and shouted, “Where do you think you are going? Go back to sleep. We shall see to it later.” The soldiers said, “If we do not leave early, the daytime heat will make it impossible to walk, and then you will beat us.” Yang Zhi cursed them furiously: “What do any of you understand?” He took up his rattan switch to beat them. The soldiers swallowed their anger and held their tongues, and had no choice but to lie down again. Not until the Hour of the Dragon did they slowly light the cooking fire, eat their meal, and set out. All along the road Yang Zhi drove and beat them, refusing to let them rest in the shade. The eleven guardsmen muttered and grumbled resentfully, while the two attendants incessantly complained about Yang Zhi before the old steward. The old steward listened without appearing to take it to heart, though inwardly he too was growing angry with Yang Zhi.

p.src: To spare needless detail, they traveled in this fashion for fourteen or fifteen days, until not one of the fourteen men was without resentment toward Yang Zhi. That day, at the Hour of the Dragon, they leisurely lit the fire at the inn, ate breakfast, and set out. It was the fourth day of the sixth month. Before noon, a red sun already hung high in a cloudless sky, and the heat that day was intense. An ancient poet composed eight lines on such heat: Zhurong comes from the south, lashing his fiery dragon; his blazing banners burn the heavens red. At noon the sun’s wheel hangs unmoving; all the nations seem enclosed within a glowing furnace. The Five Sacred Peaks are scorched bare and every cloud is gone; deep beneath the sea, the Lord of Waves fears that the waters will run dry. When will the golden autumn wind rise for a single night and sweep all this heat from the world for me?

p.src: Scorching vapors steamed the people, and clamorous dust struck their faces. The whole world for ten thousand li was like a steamer, while a single fiery parasol hung in the sky. Across the four wilds there was no cloud; the wind lay still, trees seemed to burn, and streams split dry. A thousand mountains blazed with searing flame; stones cracked and burst, scattering into ash. Birds in the air, their lives nearly spent, tumbled headlong into the depths of the woods. Fish and dragons beneath the waters, their scales and horns peeling away, bored straight into caverns deep in the mud. It would make a stone tiger pant without cease, and even an iron man drip with sweat.

p.src: Ten thousand green trees crowned its summit, while a belt of yellow sand lay at its foot. Its crags resembled the form of an ancient dragon; from its perilous heights came only the sound of wind and rain. The thatch along the mountainside, tangled strand upon strand, bristled over the ground like spears and swords. Stones covered the earth, jagged enough to resemble two rows of crouching tigers and leopards. Speak not of the dangers of the roads of Shu in Western Sichuan; know that this is the Taihang Mountains.

p.src: The party of fifteen hurried up the ridge and set down their loads and carrying poles. The other fourteen all went beneath the pines, where they collapsed and lay sleeping in the shade. Yang Zhi said, “This is disastrous! Do you know what sort of place this is, that you would rest here in the shade? Get up! Move quickly!” The soldiers said, “Even if you hack us into seven or eight pieces, we truly cannot go another step!” Yang Zhi raised the rattan switch and rained blows upon their heads and faces. No sooner had he beaten one man to his feet than another lay down again, until there was nothing he could do.

p.src: Presently the two attendants and the old steward appeared, gasping for breath. They too barely made it up the ridge, sat beneath the pines, and panted. Seeing Yang Zhi beating the soldiers, the old steward said, “Escort Officer, it truly is too hot for them to walk. Do not hold it against them.” Yang Zhi said, “Steward, you do not understand. This is precisely a haunt of bandits, a place called Yellow Clay Ridge. Even in ordinary peaceful times, they come out to rob people in broad daylight. In circumstances like these, who would dare stop here?” When the two attendants heard Yang Zhi, they said, “We have heard you say that several times already. You keep using that tale merely to frighten people!” The old steward said, “Why not let everyone rest a while for now and resume once the noonday heat has somewhat passed?” Yang Zhi said, “You too fail to understand! How could we possibly do that? Even after descending this ridge, there are still seven or eight li without a single dwelling. What sort of place do you think this is, that you dare rest here in the shade?” The old steward said, “I shall sit here for a while and then go. You may drive the others on ahead.”

p.src: Yang Zhi raised his rattan cane and shouted, “Anyone who refuses to move will taste twenty strokes from me!” All the soldiers began clamoring at once, and one of them protested, “Captain, each of us is carrying a load of a hundred catties or so; we can hardly be compared with you, walking empty-handed. You truly do not treat us as human beings! Even if His Excellency the Governor himself were escorting us, he would still let us have our say. How utterly heartless you are!” He went on arguing without pause. Yang Zhi cursed, “Will this beast not vex me to death? A beating is all he deserves!” He raised the rattan cane and struck straight at the man’s face. The old steward shouted, “Captain Yang, stop! Listen to me. When I served as a foster father in the Grand Tutor’s residence in the Eastern Capital, countless officers and soldiers under his command greeted me with one respectful assent after another. I do not say this to boast, but you were merely a condemned soldier whom His Excellency took pity on and promoted to captain—a post no bigger than a mustard seed. Is that enough to justify such swaggering? Never mind that I am steward of His Excellency’s household—even an old man from some village would deserve to have his counsel heeded. What manner of treatment is this, beating them without cease?” Yang Zhi said, “Steward, you are a city man, raised in a minister’s residence. How could you know the thousand hardships and perils of the road?” The old steward replied, “I have been to Sichuan and the Two Guangs, yet I have never seen anyone put on airs as you do.” Yang Zhi said, “These are not peaceful times now.” The steward said, “For saying such a thing, your mouth should be carved open and your tongue cut out! How can you claim the realm is not at peace today?”

p.src: When Yang Zhi came up and looked, he saw seven Jiangzhou handcarts lined abreast in the pine grove, with seven men stripped stark naked and cooling themselves there. One of them, who had a large vermilion birthmark beside his temple, took up a broad-bladed staff and came toward Yang Zhi. The seven men cried out together, “Hey!” All of them sprang to their feet. Yang Zhi shouted, “Who are you men?” The seven replied, “Who are you?” Yang Zhi asked again, “Are you not villains?” The seven said, “You have it backward, questioning us like that. We are petty traders—where would we have money to give you?” Yang Zhi said, “You may be petty traders, but do you suppose I carry some great fortune?” The seven asked, “Just who are you, then?” Yang Zhi said, “First tell me where you men come from.” The seven replied, “We seven brothers are from Haozhou. We are taking dates to sell in the Eastern Capital and happened to pass this way. We have heard many people say that bandits often rob traveling merchants here on Yellow Mud Ridge. As we walked along, we kept saying among ourselves, ‘The seven of us have only a few dates and no other valuables.’ So we kept coming over the ridge. Once atop the ridge, we could no longer endure the heat, so we stopped in this grove for a while, intending to travel on when evening brought cooler air. Then we heard people coming up the ridge. Fearing they might be villains, we sent this brother out to take a look.” Yang Zhi said, “So that is how it was. We are fellow travelers, then. Just now I saw you peering at us and feared you were villains, so I came over to investigate.” The seven men said, “Good traveler, take a few dates with you.” Yang Zhi said, “There is no need.” He lifted his broad-bladed staff and returned to the loads.

p.src: Before the time it takes to eat half a bowl of rice had passed, they saw a man in the distance carrying a pair of buckets on a shoulder pole and singing as he climbed the ridge: “The blazing red sun burns like fire; the rice in the fields lies half-parched and scorched. The farmer’s heart seethes as though in boiling broth, while noble sons and royal grandsons merely wave their fans.” Still singing, the man climbed to the top of the ridge, set down his buckets in the pine grove, and sat on the ground to cool himself. When the soldiers saw him, they asked, “What is in your buckets?” The man answered, “White wine.” The soldiers asked, “Where are you taking it?” The man said, “Out to the villages to sell.” The soldiers asked, “How much for a bucket?” The man said, “Five full strings of cash.” The soldiers conferred: “We are both hot and thirsty. Why not buy some to drink and relieve the heat?”

p.src: They were just pooling their money. Yang Zhi saw them and shouted, “What are you doing now?” The soldiers replied, “Buying a bowl of wine to drink.” Yang Zhi swung around the shaft of his broad-bladed staff and struck at them, cursing, “Without leave from me, you recklessly decide to buy wine and drink it. What audacity!” The soldiers said, “Here you come making a damned fuss again, when nothing is wrong! We are pooling our own money to buy wine. What business is it of yours? And you even strike us!” Yang Zhi said, “You village fools, what do you understand? All you care about is gratifying your mouths! You know nothing of the hazards and hardships of the road. How many brave men have been drugged senseless with knock-out powder!” The wine carrier looked at Yang Zhi and sneered, “You, good traveler, are remarkably ignorant! Fortunately, I had no intention of selling you any. Yet you come out with such feeble nonsense!”

p.src: The seven travelers said, “I thought some villains had appeared, but it was only this. There was no harm in saying so. We were just longing for some wine to quench our thirst. Since they suspect it, sell us one bucket for the time being.” The wine carrier said, “I won’t sell it! I won’t sell!” The seven travelers said, “You damned fool, you have no sense at all. We were not the ones who accused you. You are taking it to the village to sell anyway. We will pay you the same price, so why not sell us some? What harm could it do? We are not asking you to give away tea or broth; you would merely be saving us from this burning thirst.” The wine carrier then said, “I would not mind selling you a bucket, but they spoke so ill of it. Besides, there are no bowls or ladles to drink from.” The seven said, “You take things far too seriously! What harm was done by a single remark? We have coconut-shell ladles of our own.” Two of the travelers went to the carts and fetched two coconut-shell ladles, while another brought out a great handful of dates. The seven stood around the bucket, opened its lid, and took turns ladling out wine, eating dates with it. Before long, they had drained the whole bucket.

Two of the travelers went to the carts and fetched two coconut-shell ladles, while another brought out a great handful of dates.
The seven stood around the bucket, opened its lid, and took turns ladling out wine, eating dates with it.
Before long, they had drained the whole bucket.

p.src: The seven travelers said, “We never did ask how much you charge.” The man said, “I have one fixed price: five full strings of cash for a bucket, ten for a shoulder-load.” The seven said, “Five strings it is, then. Only throw in one more ladleful for us.” The man said, “I cannot. The price is fixed.” One traveler paid him, while another lifted the lid of the remaining bucket, scooped up a ladleful, and raised it to his lips. When the man tried to snatch it away, the traveler fled toward the pine grove with half a ladleful of wine still in his hand, and the man chased after him. Just then another traveler emerged from the pine grove carrying a ladle, came to the bucket, and scooped up a ladleful of wine. Seeing this, the man rushed back, tore it from his hand, poured it into the bucket, clapped on the lid, and flung the ladle to the ground, crying, “What a dishonorable fellow you are! A respectable-looking man like you, making such a nuisance of yourself!”

p.src: Watching from across the way, the soldiers began to crave the wine, and one of them appealed to the old superintendent: “Honored sir, please say a word for us. Those date merchants bought and drank a whole bucket. Let us buy this one somehow and moisten our throats. We truly are parched with heat and can bear it no longer. There is nowhere on this ridge to get water. Please show us mercy, sir.” Hearing the soldiers, the old superintendent—who wanted some himself—went straight to Yang Zhi and said, “Those date merchants have already bought and drunk one bucket of his wine. Only this bucket remains. Let the men buy some to ward off the heat. There truly is nowhere on this ridge to find water.” Yang Zhi thought, “From a distance I watched these fellows buy and drink his wine, and I also saw half a ladleful from this very bucket drunk before my eyes. It must be safe. I have beaten them half the day; I may as well let them buy a bowlful.” Yang Zhi said, “Since the old superintendent has spoken, let these wretches buy and drink it. Then we leave at once.”

p.src: Delighted, the soldiers pooled five full strings of cash and came to buy the wine. The wine seller said, “It is no longer for sale! No longer for sale! There is sleeping potion in this wine!” The soldiers smiled ingratiatingly and said, “Brother, must you throw our own words back at us?” The man said, “It is not for sale! Stop pestering me!” The date merchants urged him, “You damned fool, they spoke out of turn, but you take it far too seriously! Even we had to endure several harsh words from you because of it. The others had nothing to do with it. Just sell them some to drink.” The man said, “Why invite suspicion for no reason?” The date merchants pushed the wine seller aside and simply carried the bucket over for the soldiers to drink. The soldiers opened the lid, but had nothing with which to scoop the wine. Speaking most politely, they asked to borrow the travelers’ coconut-shell ladles. The travelers said, “We will give you these few dates to go with the wine as well.” The soldiers thanked them, saying, “You really need not do that.” The travelers said, “No need for thanks. We are all travelers alike; what does a hundred or so dates matter?” After thanking them, the soldiers first scooped out two ladlefuls, offering one to the old superintendent and one to Commandant Yang, but Yang Zhi refused to drink. The old superintendent drank one ladleful first, and the two deputies each drank one as well. Then all the soldiers crowded forward, and the bucket was drained in an instant.

p.src: When Yang Zhi saw that nothing had happened to the others, though he had not intended to drink, the fierce heat and unbearable thirst overcame him. He took the ladle, drank only half of it, and ate a few of the dates. The wine seller said, “That traveler stole a ladleful from this bucket, so you received less wine. I will take half a string of cash off the price.” The soldiers pooled their money and paid him. The man took the money, shouldered the empty buckets, and went down the ridge as before, singing a mountain song.

p.src: The seven date merchants stood beside the pines, pointed at the fifteen men, and cried, “Fall down! Fall down!” At once the fifteen felt their heads grow heavy and their feet light. They stared at one another and collapsed helplessly, one after another. The seven travelers pushed their seven Jiangzhou handcarts out of the pine grove, dumped the dates on the ground, loaded all eleven loads of gold, pearls, and treasure into the carts, and covered them securely. With a shout of “Forgive the disturbance!” they pushed the carts straight down Yellow Mud Ridge. Truly:

p.src: They wrung blood and fat from the people to celebrate a birthday, heedless that common lives stood next to death. Now we know such acts have always summoned robbers; a guilty heart is certain to reap the fate it has sown.

p.src: Yang Zhi could only groan in despair. His body had gone limp, and struggle as he might, he could not rise; the fifteen men watched helplessly as the seven loaded up all the gold and treasure and carried it away, but they could not rise, move, or speak.

p.src: Now let me ask you: who, in truth, were those seven men? They were none other than Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Liu Tang, and the three Ruan brothers. And the fellow carrying the wine was none other than Bai Sheng, known as the “Daylight Rat.” But how had they administered the drug? When the buckets were carried up the ridge, both contained perfectly good wine. The seven first drank one bucket. Then Liu Tang lifted the lid of the other and deliberately scooped out half a ladleful to drink where the guards could see him, solely to dispel every last suspicion. Afterward, Wu Yong went into the pine grove, fetched the drug, and shook it into his ladle. Pretending to come back and steal a free drink, he dipped the ladle into the bucket, mixing the drug into the wine. He feigned drinking half a ladleful, whereupon Bai Sheng snatched it away and poured it back into the bucket. That was the trick. The entire scheme had been devised by Wu Yong. This is known as “Outwitting the Guards to Seize the Birthday Gifts.”

p.src: Because Yang Zhi had drunk little wine, he awoke sooner. He struggled to his feet, though he still could not keep his balance. When he looked at the other fourteen, he saw drool running from their mouths and none of them able to move—just as the proverb says: “Cunning as a ghost you may be, yet you have drunk the water used to wash another’s feet.”

p.src: Yang Zhi said bitterly, “It is not merely that you have taken the Birthday Gifts—how can I go back and face Grand Secretary Liang? I can never hand in this receipt now, so I may as well tear it up. Now I have been left with no home to return to and no country in which to seek refuge. Where can I possibly go? I would be better off finding a place to die right here on this ridge.” Gathering up his robe, he broke into a run and made to leap down from Yellow Mud Ridge. Indeed:
